response.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT pr.product_id, pc.product_type_description AS d, AVG(CAST(oi.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS q, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS c FROM Products pr JOIN Product_Categories pc ON pc.production_type_code = pr.production_type_code LEFT JOIN Order_Items oi ON oi.product_id = pr.product_id GROUP BY pr.product_id, pc.product_type_description), s AS (SELECT d, q, c, c * 1.0 / SUM(c) OVER () AS sh FROM p), t AS (SELECT d, AVG(q) AS aq, AVG(c) AS ac, AVG(sh) AS ash FROM s GROUP BY d) SELECT AVG(aq) AS avg_quantity, AVG(ac) AS avg_order_item_count, AVG(ash) AS avg_share FROM t

assumptions.assumption: product_quantity is a VARCHAR holding numeric text, so it is cast to a number before averaging. Non-numeric or missing values are ignored.
Product types are grouped by product_type_description, as the request says. Categories that share a description are merged into one type.
The total for the share is the sum of order-item counts over all products. Every order item references a product, so this equals the total number of order items.
